defects: Moves the quantifier over immersions: gold takes a single GIVEN immersion φ (with hφ : IsImmersionOfComplement ... φ) as an external parameter, so the iff is stated for one fixed immersion; produced instead places '∀ P g, IsImmersion g → ContMDiff (g∘f)' inside the RHS of the iff, which is a different (and stronger/degenerate) logical statement, not equivalent to the gold's per-immersion family of iffs.

Drops the key hypothesis 'IsImmersionOfComplement' (an immersion with a locally split/complemented normal bundle, essential for the backward direction of the theorem) and substitutes the strictly weaker plain 'Manifold.IsImmersion', losing the structural condition that makes the equivalence provable.

Forces the further manifold P (and even N) to share the exact same model I and chart space H as M, via 'ChartedSpace H P', 'IsManifold I n P', and 'Manifold.IsImmersion I I n g' — whereas gold allows a genuinely different model (J, J', E''', G', F) for the target/further manifold, matching the informal statement's 'a further manifold' (arbitrary manifold, not same-model).

Because the produced RHS quantifies over ALL immersions g rather than one witness, it admits a degenerate instantiation (e.g. P = N, g = id_N, which is a valid immersion) that makes the RHS conjunct 'ContMDiff (g∘f)' reduce to 'ContMDiff f' directly, trivializing the intended content that a single well-chosen immersion suffices to detect smoothness.

No analogue of the 'F' (complement space) parameter appears in the produced statement, so the necessary splitting/complement data used to characterize which immersions make the criterion work is entirely absent.
